[5] Key discussions focused on data-driven climate action, upcoming environmental legislation, sustainable material innovation, and developing circular systems to reduce the industry's carbon footprint. In an announcement on August 15, 2023, the company stated it would showcase its new product line for the 2023/24 winter season. <8> A report from July 24, 2023, detailed the significant and increasing focus on environmental sustainability among North American ski resorts. A key initiative highlighted is Vail Resorts' "Epic Promise for a Zero Footprint," which aims for zero net emissions, zero waste to landfill, and zero net operating impact on forests and habitat by 2030. metadata.original_text: This time series records ski gear data in the web search domain, with a collection frequency of weekly, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2024-07-07 to 2024-09-22. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On June 27, 2024, the U.S. Ski & Snowboard and X Games announced a strategic partnership to create 'The Winter X Games Series.' This collaboration will integrate U.S. Ski & Snowboard's FIS World Cup events, specifically the Toyota U.S. Grand Prix and Visa Big Air, with the X Games competition framework. The partnership aims to elevate freeskiing and snowboarding by creating a clearer pathway for athletes to advance to the X Games; winners of the specified World Cup events will now receive guaranteed invitations. Additionally, athletes in the Revolution Tour, a U.S. Ski & Snowboard development series, will have an opportunity to qualify. The collaboration, which is part of a broader expansion by X Games that includes a new league format debuting in 2026, will also involve co-branding, content sharing, and adding X Games disciplines like knuckle huck and street style to U.S. World Cup weekends. <2> The owners of Beartooth Basin, America's only summer-exclusive ski area, have put the resort up for sale. Situated at 10,900 feet in the Beartooth Mountains of Montana near the Wyoming border, the ski area typically opens from late May through July. The decision to sell follows two challenging seasons, including a very short 2023 season and not opening at all in 2024 due to insufficient snowpack. The sale includes two surface lifts, snowcats, and other operational equipment, along with a 20-year permit from the Forest Service. Co-owner Austin Hart stated the ownership group feels they have improved the operation and wants to pass the opportunity to new owners with the resources to help the ski area reach its full potential. <3> Black Diamond Equipment, in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) and Health Canada, issued a voluntary recall for its bright green 2024 Neve Strap Crampons and associated accessory kits. The specific products affected are the Neve Strap Crampons (style #400073), the Neve Strap Binding Accessory Kit (style #400683), and the Neve Strap Heel Cup Screw & Nuts (style #400687), all sold between January and May 2024. The recall was initiated because screws connecting the plastic heel cup to the aluminum heel unit can loosen, allowing the heel cup to detach and creating a significant fall hazard. This recall applies to products with date codes 01-2021, 05-2022, 07-2023, 01-2024, and SS1271. There were three reported incidents of the heel cup detaching, though no injuries were reported. Consumers are advised to immediately stop using the products and contact Black Diamond for a full refund. <4> Ski brand Dynastar announced on May 6, 2024, the return of its Race Test Center to Government Camp, Oregon. The center provided athletes the opportunity to test the new 2024-25 race collection, including updated Speed World Cup and Speed Omeglass FIS SL skis. The event ran from June 10th to June 29th, 2024, allowing athletes to gain firsthand experience with the latest innovations from Dynastar's Race Department and interact with company experts for personalized advice. <5> Fischer Sports issued a voluntary recall for its RC4 Junior ski boot models—specifically the RC4 50, RC4 60, and RC4 65 in sizes 21.5 to 27.5—due to a potential malfunction. The recall, announced in conjunction with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, addresses an issue where the boot's cuff can unexpectedly rotate backward, creating a fall hazard and risk of injury for the user. Approximately 1,460 units in the U.S. and 114 in Canada are affected by this recall. The recalled boots were sold nationwide in ski gear stores and online from October 2022 through February 2024. One incident of a ski boot cuff rotating has been reported, though no injuries have occurred. Consumers are advised to immediately stop using the recalled boots and contact Fischer Sports for a free repair, replacement, or refund. <6> Ikon Pass announced its 2024-2025 pass details on March 7, 2024, with passes going on sale March 14, 2024. [2, 3] The updated pass offerings include several new benefits to enhance value for the upcoming ski season. Pass holders will now receive a total of 12 'Friends & Family' discounts, an increase of two from the previous season, each providing at least 25% off daily lift tickets. [1, 6] Additionally, each Ikon Pass, Ikon Base Pass, and Ikon Base Plus Pass will include one complimentary summer bike park lift ticket valid at select resorts. [1] For those seeking a heli-skiing adventure, a credit of up to $1,400 CAD towards a CMH Heli-Skiing trip is also a new feature. [1] Renewal discounts of up to $100 are available for returning pass holders for a limited time. [2] <7> In a move to combat microplastic pollution, global outdoor apparel brand The North Face has partnered with the BOTTLE (Bio-Optimized Technologies to keep Thermoplastics out of Landfills and the Environment) Consortium, a research initiative funded by the U.S. Department of Energy. [1, 2] The collaboration, announced on February 29, 2024, will focus on scaling up the production of polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs), a biodegradable and bio-based alternative to conventional polyester. [1, 4] Unlike petroleum-derived polyesters, which are a major source of microplastic pollution, PHAs can break down naturally in the environment without requiring highly controlled composting conditions. [1, 4, 6] Over the next year, the BOTTLE Consortium, spearheaded by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), will produce several pounds of PHA fiber. [1, 2] The North Face will then conduct rigorous testing and evaluation on these fibers for potential incorporation into its product lines, aiming to create more sustainable outdoor apparel with a smaller environmental footprint. [1, 2] BOTTLE scientists have already developed PHAs that mimic the properties of polyester and are also designed to be chemically recyclable, allowing the material to be broken down to its basic building blocks and reused, in principle, infinitely. [1] <8> A study conducted by the University of Waterloo and the University of Innsbruck revealed that the U.S. ski industry incurred losses exceeding $5 billion between 2000 and 2019 due to human-caused climate change. This figure stems from an average annual cost of $252 million, attributed to lost skier visits and increased snowmaking expenses as the average ski season shortened by five to seven days compared to the 1960-1979 baseline. The research, published in the journal *Current Issues in Tourism*, projects that by the 2050s, annual economic damages could rise to $657 million under a low-emission scenario or as high as $1.4 billion if emissions remain high. These future scenarios also predict ski seasons could shorten by 14 to 33 days in a low-emission future and 27 to 62 days in a high-emission future, even with advanced snowmaking. Researchers note these estimates are conservative as they do not factor in broader economic impacts on ski tourism communities, such as losses in lodging and retail. <9> A report from Grand View Research indicates that the U.S. skiing and snowboarding market was valued at USD 5.53 billion in 2023. [3] The report forecasts a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.0% from 2024 to 2030, projecting the market to reach USD 7.74 billion by 2030. [1, 3] This growth is attributed to the increasing number of snow sports tournaments and events, which boosts interest and drives sales of specialized equipment. [3] The equipment segment, including items like skis, snowboards, and safety gear, accounted for over 46% of the market's revenue in 2023. [3] The skiing segment alone represented more than 68% of total revenues in the same year. [1, 3] <10> BRP (Bombardier Recreational Products) issued a safety recall for approximately 8,100 of its 2024 Ski-Doo MXZ and Renegade snowmobiles in the United States, along with about 5,600 units in Canada. The recall, announced by BRP on January 31, 2024, addresses a manufacturing defect in the left Pilot X ski, which can break due to a molding process issue at a supplier. This defect poses a significant safety risk, as a broken ski could lead to a loss of control and potentially cause a crash, resulting in serious injury or death. Prior to the recall, there were 27 reports of the left ski breaking in the U.S., with no resulting injuries. However, one incident in Canada resulted in an injury. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) officially announced the recall on February 29, 2024. BRP is contacting all registered owners and instructing them to stop using the affected snowmobiles immediately and to contact an authorized dealer for a free inspection and replacement of the left ski.
